title: Globe outline sheet and UK seas map
subject: Geography
source: Written for geography/y4 lesson 13 (Globe outline sheet and UK seas map (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 13: Seas, the Equator and the hemispheres. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.text: Draw the equator across the middle of your globe and label the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.

panels.title: Seas around the UK
points: Atlantic Ocean to the north and west

panels.title: The Equator
points: A line round the middle of Earth
Splits Earth into northern and southern halves
Places near it are hot all year

panels.title: Four hemispheres
points: Northern and Southern: split by the Equator
Eastern and Western: split by the Prime Meridian
The Prime Meridian runs through Greenwich, London

model.title: Why is June cold in Australia?

parts.text: In June the north leans towards the Sun
Less sunlight means winter in the south

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: The Southern Hemisphere has winter in June

keywords.def: a smaller area of salt water, often part of an ocean
an imaginary line round the middle of the Earth
an imaginary line through Greenwich, London, from pole to pole
how far north or south of the Equator a place is

questions.q: Which sea separates England and France?
Is Australia north or south of the Equator?
Core: On the globe map sheet, draw and label the Equator and the Prime Meridian, label the four hemispheres, and mark the UK and Australia.
questions.a: Lines and labels correct; UK in the north and east/west, Australia in the south and east

questions.q: Extend: Label the four seas and ocean around the UK.
questions.a: North Sea, Irish Sea, English Channel, Atlantic Ocean

questions.q: Stretch: Why are places near the Equator hot all year?
questions.a: The Sun is high in the sky all year, so sunlight is strong
B) Northern Hemisphere. The UK is north of the Equator, so it is in the Northern Hemisphere.

questions.q: Big question: is it summer everywhere in June?
questions.a: No: June is summer in the north but winter in the south
